comparison: Perfect agreement. Both evaluations cover identical claims (C40-C47, C50-C53) regarding genetic evidence from Figure 3, including null allele characterization, phenotypic analysis, and rescue experiments. Both conclude the data strongly support that only Dally is required for Dpp signaling with appropriate controls demonstrating specificity.

Strong agreement on overlapping claims (C35, C37, C39) regarding differential effects of Dally vs Dlp overexpression on Dpp distribution. OpenEval additionally evaluates C36 and C112 (internal controls). Both conclude the data support that only Dally interacts with Dpp.

Strong agreement on overlapping claims (C72-C75, C78-C80) regarding genetic epistasis experiments from Figure 6. Both conclude the data support that Dally-HS antagonizes Tkv-mediated Dpp internalization. OpenEval additionally evaluates C76-C77 regarding pMad upregulation in ventral cells.

Strong agreement on overlapping claims (C66-C71) regarding dppΔN characterization and its mild phenotypes contrasting with dallyΔHS. Both conclude the data challenge the prevailing model and support that HS chains function without directly binding Dpp. OpenEval additionally evaluates C63-C65 regarding rescue strategy.

Strong agreement on overlapping claims (C55-C59) regarding DallyΔHS binding Dpp but failing to activate signaling. Peer review additionally evaluates C60-C62 regarding endogenous expression validation. Both describe this as critical evidence supporting the two-component model of Dally function.

Partial overlap. OpenEval R4 evaluates C60-C62 regarding physiological validation of DallyΔHS at endogenous levels. Peer R3 covers these claims as part of a broader evaluation that also includes C55-C59 and C66-C71. Both agree the endogenous DallyΔHS data provide strong support for the model.

Strong agreement on overlapping claims (C86, C88, C89) regarding rejection of facilitated/hindered diffusion models. Both conclude the data support that Dally does not mediate Dpp internalization/recycling. OpenEval additionally evaluates C85 and C87 regarding alternative binding factors.

Minimal overlap on C105 (negative conclusion about Dally not mediating internalization). OpenEval R11 rates this as UNCERTAIN due to speculative claims about Pent-Dally interaction (C106-C109), while Peer R6 focuses on the supported negative conclusion and broader model acceptance.

Both address C81 regarding general principles of glypican function. OpenEval evaluates C81-C84 as SUPPORTED conceptual synthesis, noting it's inferential rather than directly tested. Peer review evaluates C3-C5 and C81, accepting the overall model as consistent with results.

OpenEval evaluates C91-C94 regarding HS chains functioning without binding Dpp and speculation about direct HS-Tkv interaction. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though the broader model is accepted in peer R7.

OpenEval evaluates C95-C104 providing detailed critique of Romanova-Michaelides et al. (2022) regarding overexpression artifacts and alternative explanations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this specific scientific disagreement.
OpenEval evaluates C110-C111 regarding conceptual framework about high receptor affinity limiting morphogen range. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this general principle synthesis.

OpenEval evaluates C22-C34 summarizing existing models from literature with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background/literature review claims.
